gaps.title: No application-supplied, input-aware authorization hook in FeltKit
gaps.description: FeltKit evaluates every boundary (HTTP functions, /appport, MCP, Services) through one AppPort Authorizer built from application-wide roles. An application cannot add a policy that decides on the call's input ("may this caller act on workspace W / channel C"). AppPort already supports exactly this: AuthorizationRequest carries the validated `input` 'so policies can make resource-aware decisions', and combineAuthorizers/authorizerFrom compose policies. FeltKit does not expose it.
evidence: @feltdb/feltkit 0.3.15 dist/app.d.ts: FeltKitOptions has roles, auth.authenticate, dev, services, agent, activity; no authorize/authorizer option

@feltdb/feltkit dist/runtime/authority.d.ts: Authority(applicationId, roles) — role → permission only; authorize({access, principal, target, transport, input}) receives input but evaluates permissionAuthorizer
@appport/authorization dist/index.d.ts: AuthorizationRequest.input ('Validated capability input, so policies can make resource-aware decisions'); combineAuthorizers; authorizerFrom
@appport/authorization: AuthorizationContext doc: 'Handlers use it for resource-level checks that the declarative capability permissions cannot express'
gaps.wanted: Declare once, beside roles, that functions taking a workspaceId/channelId/messageId require membership, and have the decision recorded by AppPort with a decision id on every interface.
gaps.provided: Role/permission checks at every boundary; ctx.auth.require(permission) inside handlers.
gaps.implementedManually: feltkit/_authz.ts: loads the target record from the id the client sent, resolves the caller's participant and membership, and refuses NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN. Called at the top of every handler that takes an id.
gaps.workaround: Centralized helper module called explicitly by each handler; transport-independent (runs inside the function, so HTTP, AppPort and MCP calls all pass through it).
gaps.customLoc: 51 (feltkit/_authz.ts) + 43 call sites in handlers = ~94 code lines. Of these ~20 lines of plumbing (load record → resolve workspace → find membership) and the 43 call sites would disappear; ~30 lines of membership policy are application-specific and would relocate into the registered authorizer. — MEASURED after the primitive (consumer run): net +39 lines; 37 call sites remain as loaders. See resolution.measuredEffect.
gaps.estimatedHours: 2–3 h (design + every handler + 9 security tests' worth of cases)
gaps.codeFate: Relocates and gains guarantees; does not shrink Multiplayer (measured).
gaps.proposal: feltkit({ authorize: Authorizer | (req: { principal, function, capability, input, db }) => Decision }) composed after the role authorizer with combineAuthorizers, given a read-only db handle on the same instance, applied identically at HTTP, AppPort, MCP and Services boundaries, and recorded like role denials. Per-function opt-in: app.query({ access, resource: (args) => ({ type: 'channel', id: args.channelId }) }).
gaps.owner: FeltKit (exposes AppPort's existing Authorizer composition); AppPort unchanged
gaps.status: implemented in FeltKit (local commit f20ed78, unreleased); consumer acceptance passed
gaps.codeKind: platform integration glue (call sites, plumbing) + application policy (rules)

resolution.missing: A way for an application to supply an input-aware decision composed with FeltKit's role policy at every boundary.
resolution.existed: AppPort's Authorizer contract already carries the validated input ('so policies can make resource-aware decisions') and AuthorizationDecision; FeltKit's Authority already passed `input` but evaluated roles only. Every interface (HTTP /api, AppPort, MCP, agent actions, jobs) already funnels into Runtime#call; the AppBoundry guest has the same call path.
reused: the call's own ctx.db reader (read fences at commit; live-query read set)
implemented: src/authorize.ts: AuthorizeHook/AuthorizeRequest/AuthorizeResult, evaluateAuthorize (fail closed, read-only db view) — runtime-neutral, shared by runtime and guest
Runtime#call: hook after roles + validation, before the handler, inside each attempt (re-evaluated on sequence retries); authority.resource recorded
AppBoundry guest: the same hook at the same point
Docs: README, GUARANTEES (table), CHANGELOG, feltkit-build skill; UPSTREAM-GAPS A8/A9
resolution.publicApi: feltkit({ authorize?: (req: { function, kind, access, capability?, principal, args, transport, requestId, db }) => boolean | AuthorizationDecision | Promise<…> }); exported types AuthorizeHook, AuthorizeRequest, AuthorizeResult; activity entry authority.resource { allowed, reason? }. Additive: no change for apps without it.
tests: packages/sdk/test/authorize.test.ts: 10 tests — decision from args + stored records; order (roles → validation → hook); AppPort dispatch; a real MCP client; denial evidence incl. NOT_FOUND concealment; commit fence (membership revoked mid-call → CONFLICT, nothing written); live read set; a real live-query client denied on revocation; fail closed (throw / garbage / write attempt); the compiled AppBoundry artifact
resolution.consumer: acceptance/feltkit-authorize/run.sh: local FeltKit packed into a scratch copy of Multiplayer; Multiplayer's 18 tests pass unchanged (no regression), and pass again with the whole membership policy in one feltkit({ authorize }) hook while _authz.ts's requireWorkspace/requireChannel enforce nothing.
resolution.measuredEffect: Code size did not shrink: _authz.ts 51 → 45 lines, hook +45, net +39; 37 call sites remain as context loaders (participant, role, channel). The gain is guarantees: one policy on every function and interface, default-deny for functions the policy does not recognise, decision fenced at commit, live revocation, recorded decisions. The earlier estimate (≈63 lines disappear) was wrong and is corrected here.
remaining: A central hook relies on argument naming (Multiplayer's presence:heartbeat names its channel `typingIn`; the first consumer run caught it). Proposal: optional per-function `resource: (args) => ({ type, id })` declaration so the policy does not infer from names.
AppPort decisions cannot express NOT_FOUND (AppPort A9); FeltKit accepts fail('NOT_FOUND') from the hook.

Unverified on the real AppBoundry runtime (@appport/appboundry): the guest change ships in the artifact, but the published runtime was not rebuilt with it here; FeltKit's reference host (createArtifactTestApp) passes.

gaps.title: AuthBoundry has no resource-level evaluation, and FeltKit has no AuthBoundry adapter
gaps.description: AuthBoundry models tenancy, principals, agents and delegation, but its enforcement contract evaluates at capability granularity only: `resource` is recorded as evidence, not evaluated. FeltKit has no adapter to AuthBoundry at all (no source references to @authboundry); the adapter is a planned step blocked on verifying a published release.
evidence: authboundry docs/ENFORCEMENT.md 'Not covered yet': 'Resource-level evaluation. `resource` is recorded as evidence. Application decisions are evaluated at capability granularity'
feltkit docs/AGENT-OPERATIONS.md: '4: AuthBoundry adapter … whether delegations, agent credentials and runs under a delegation are in 1.15.3 is unverified'
grep -r @authboundry packages/sdk/src → no matches (FeltKit 50bc617)
gaps.wanted: Tenant (workspace) membership and per-resource decisions owned by the authority boundary, with delegation for agents acting for a person.
gaps.provided: Nothing reachable from a FeltKit app.
gaps.implementedManually: Same code as FK-GAP-001 (_authz.ts) plus app-owned memberships collection.
gaps.workaround: Application-owned membership records in FeltDB; app-level checks.
gaps.codeFate: Would move membership records and policy to AuthBoundry; requires FK-GAP-001's hook as the integration point.
gaps.proposal: AuthBoundry: evaluate `resource` (not only record it). FeltKit: an adapter that implements AuthorizeHook by calling AuthBoundry enforce/decide with { principal, capability, resource } — plugs into the hook from FK-GAP-001 with no further FeltKit API.
gaps.status: open — FeltKit integration point now exists (feltkit({ authorize })); AuthBoundry resource evaluation still missing

gaps.title: No tenancy / membership primitive
gaps.description: FeltKit roles are application-wide: a principal holds the same roles everywhere. Multi-tenant apps (workspaces, organizations, projects) must model tenants, memberships, per-tenant roles and invitations themselves.
evidence: feltkit README 'Identity and authority': roles map to permission strings for the whole application
docs/GUARANTEES.md: 'FeltKit is single-tenant per application'
gaps.wanted: Workspaces with per-workspace roles and invitations.
gaps.implementedManually: workspaces, memberships, invitations collections and their functions.
gaps.customLoc: ~147: memberships + invitations collections (~25), invitations.ts (75), workspaces setRole/removeMember (33), _ops addToWorkspace/joinChannel (14). Roughly 110 are reusable tenancy mechanics (membership, role-in-tenant, invitation lifecycle); ~35 are workspace semantics that stay.
gaps.codeFate: Partly application-specific (what a workspace is), partly reusable (membership, role-in-tenant, invitation lifecycle). A primitive would remove the reusable part.
gaps.proposal: Optional `app.tenancy({ collection, roles })` primitive: membership + invitation records and a `ctx.tenant` resolved per call, feeding FK-GAP-001.
gaps.owner: AuthBoundry (membership as delegation), with FeltKit integration through FK-GAP-001/002 — not a FeltKit membership store
gaps.status: open — reassigned to AuthBoundry; FeltKit side now available (authorize hook)
gaps.ownershipEvidence: authboundry docs/PHASE_PRODUCT_12_CUSTOMER_IDENTITY_TENANT_LIFECYCLE.md: 'Use AuthBoundry's delegation model for customer-to-organization membership, not a separate RBAC system.' A FeltKit tenancy store would duplicate it.

gaps.title: No ephemeral / broadcast real-time primitive (presence, typing)
gaps.description: The only real-time channel is the change stream: it carries the names of collections FeltDB committed to, and clients re-run queries. Nothing carries short-lived state that should not be a durable commit (presence, typing, cursors).
evidence: packages/sdk/src/runtime/changes.ts header: change feed read from FeltDB's operation journal, events name collections
packages/sdk/src/client/index.ts #connect: SSE events 'change' {collections}, 'ready', 'reload' only
grep presence|ephemeral|broadcast|typing in packages/sdk/src → none
gaps.wanted: Presence and typing indicators that are not durable records.
gaps.implementedManually: presence collection: one overwritten record per (workspace, participant), heartbeat and typing mutations; client-side expiry.
gaps.workaround: Bounded durable record (never grows), so delivery works on every FeltKit target including AppBoundry without a second transport. Cost: each heartbeat/keystroke burst is a FeltDB commit and an activity entry, and every client watching presence re-queries.
gaps.customLoc: ~55: presence.ts (19), presence collection (~8), presence fields in workspaces:get (~6), client heartbeat/typing/expiry in Workspace.tsx (22). ~40 would disappear with an ephemeral channel; the UI rendering stays.
gaps.codeFate: Mostly disappears: a platform `ctx.ephemeral.publish(topic, value, { ttl })` with authorized subscription would replace the collection, heartbeat mutation and expiry logic; the UI stays.
gaps.proposal: An authorized ephemeral channel on the existing /api/events stream: publish(topic, payload, ttl) from functions, subscribe(topic) from clients, topics authorized by FK-GAP-001's hook; never written to FeltDB.
gaps.owner: AppPort (events: authorization + scope) first; then FeltKit integration (ctx publish + client subscribe on AppPort events)
gaps.status: partially addressed — AppPort prerequisite implemented locally (f1f8c21, unreleased); FeltKit integration blocked on an AppPort release (publishing needs approval)

resolution.existed: AppPort events: defineEvent (with authorization), subscribe/unsubscribe/event envelopes, at-most-once EventBus ('nothing is buffered for absent subscribers'), WebSocket and SSE (/appport/events) delivery. This is the ephemeral channel; FeltKit should not build another.
resolution.defectFound: AppPort delivered events a session may not observe: a '*' subscription required nothing and received every event (spec §21.7 violated), and subscriptions were checked against session.permissions only (never the application's Authorizer), so principal-identified connections could not subscribe to permissioned events. Events had no scope, so per-tenant events would reach every tenant. Reproduced by packages/server/test/subscriptions.test.ts before the fix.
implemented: AppPortApplication.authorizeObservation (the application's Authorizer decides: event as capability, declared permissions as required, { scope } as input)
AppPortConnection: exact subscriptions authorized when made; every delivery re-authorized (wildcard leak closed; revocation applies to live subscriptions)
Scoped events: optional `scope` on event/subscribe envelopes (validated; spec §9.3/§9.4 and envelope JSON schema), EmitEventInput.scope, EventFilter.scope; SSE ?scope=
tests: packages/server/test/subscriptions.test.ts: 5 tests incl. a real HTTP SSE stream
AppPort full suite: 1812 passed, 1 skipped (baseline 1807 passed, 1 skipped)
remaining: FeltKit integration: declare events in feltkit({...}), publish from functions with scope, client subscribe; the FeltKit authorize hook then decides scopes (e.g. workspace membership).
AppPort client/transport API to pass `scope` (protocol and server done; client SDK not changed).
Compatibility: an AppPort app with no authorizer (publicOnlyAuthorizer) can no longer open permissioned subscriptions from session.permissions alone.

gaps.title: Live-query invalidation is per collection, not per query predicate
gaps.description: A query re-runs when any record in any collection it read changes. One message in #random re-runs every open channel's message query, every thread and every unread count, for every connected client.
evidence: packages/sdk/src/client/index.ts watchQuery: reruns when `collections.some((c) => reads.has(c))`
README 'Live queries': 'streams the names of changed collections'
gaps.wanted: Clients notified only when their channel changes.
gaps.provided: Collection-level invalidation, at-least-once within ~150 ms (local) / ~1 s (FeltDB server).
gaps.implementedManually: Nothing (accepted); recorded as a scaling limit.
gaps.workaround: None needed at demo scale. Mitigation would be one collection per channel, which FeltKit's schema model does not allow dynamically.
gaps.proposal: Carry equality predicates (collection + indexed field values) in the change event and in a query's recorded reads, so watchQuery matches on (collection, channelId).
gaps.owner: FeltKit (change feed); FeltDB (F7 change listener naming keys)

gaps.title: No text search / contains operator in ctx.db.query
gaps.description: WhereClause supports eq, neq, lt, lte, gt, gte only. Message search has to read the workspace's messages and filter in the handler.
evidence: packages/sdk/src/runtime/data.ts:50 interface WhereClause { field; eq; neq; lt; lte; gt; gte }
gaps.wanted: Search messages across the conversations the caller can read.
gaps.implementedManually: messages:search scans the workspace's messages, filters by readable channels and a case-insensitive substring match.
gaps.workaround: Bounded scan in the handler (O(messages in workspace)).
gaps.customLoc: ~18 (messages:search). ~10 (scan + match) would disappear with an indexed text predicate; readable-channel filtering stays.
gaps.codeFate: Filtering by readable channels stays (authorization); the scan and matching would disappear with an indexed text predicate.
gaps.proposal: A `contains`/`prefix` predicate and an optional text index declaration in app.collection(..., { search: ['text'] }).

gaps.title: Files are application-shared; per-resource file access must be bound by the app
gaps.description: Any principal with files.read can read every file. Attaching a file to a conversation, and authorizing reads by that conversation, is the application's job. There is also no browser download/upload route for files: bytes cross the function API (base64 in JSON).
evidence: feltkit docs/GUARANTEES.md:269 'Files are application-shared: any principal with files.read reads every file.'
runtime/services.ts FilesWriter.upload(content: string | Uint8Array); maxBytes 1 MiB default (GUARANTEES.md:156)
server/*: no /api/files route; admin.ts file routes are behind the admin token
gaps.wanted: Upload a file into a channel; only channel members can download it.
gaps.provided: Files service: upload/list/get/read/remove with metadata, authorized by app-wide permission.
gaps.implementedManually: attachments collection binding fileId → channel; upload/download functions with membership checks; base64 transfer.
gaps.workaround: Bind in app; transfer base64 through functions (1 MiB cap).
gaps.customLoc: ~78: _base64.ts (23), attachments.ts (38), attachments collection (~12), client base64/Blob conversions (~5). ~30 (base64 transfer) disappear with a signed file route; the channel binding (~45) is application semantics and stays.
gaps.codeFate: Binding record stays (it's app semantics); base64 plumbing disappears with a signed download URL; the authorization moves into FK-GAP-001's hook if Files consulted it.
gaps.proposal: Files: authorize reads through the app's resource authorizer (metadata-based), and a signed, short-lived download/upload URL issued by a function.
gaps.owner: AppPort Services (authorization by metadata, signed URLs); FeltKit (route)

gaps.title: No hosted, event-triggered execution for application agents
gaps.description: FeltKit's agent decides among options a mutation offers (ctx.agent.start) or works operator tasks in Studio; external agents connect over MCP with a session. There is no way for an application to run its own room agent in response to an event (a mention) under the agent's own identity. ctx.agent is refused by the AppBoundry build.
evidence: README 'Agents': 'There is no planner: playbooks choose capabilities by code, models choose among options code built, and open-ended work is an external agent's.'
README AppBoundry: build refuses ctx.agent
jobs run 'as the principal that created them' (README Services) — a job queued by a person runs with the person's authority, not the agent's
gaps.wanted: @assistant mention → the agent reads the conversation and acts, as itself, through the app's capabilities.
gaps.provided: Agent sessions (feltkit session create --type agent), capabilities over AppPort/MCP, the change stream.
gaps.implementedManually: agentRequests queue (durable), agent:* capabilities (pending/claim/context/respond), and an external worker process (agent/room-agent.ts) authenticated with an agent session.
gaps.workaround: External worker adapter. Durable queue makes it crash-safe; the worker holds no state.
gaps.customLoc: ~133: agentRequests collection (~17), agents.ts queue functions pending/claim/failRequest/requests (50), mention→request in messages:send (~8), agent/worker.ts (31), agent/room-agent.ts (27). ~110 would disappear with platform agent triggers; agent/compose.ts (69) is the agent's behaviour and stays.
gaps.codeFate: Queue/claim/lease plumbing disappears with a platform 'agent trigger' (run handler X as principal P when event E). The agent's behaviour (compose summary/plan) stays application code.
gaps.proposal: app.agent('assistant', { principal, roles, on: 'messages.mention', handler }) executed by FeltKit's runtime (and AppBoundry's) as the agent principal, with at-least-once delivery and leases.

gaps.title: AppBoundry deployment (Hetzner) is not available to an application
gaps.description: The FeltKit → AppBoundry deploy contract is implemented and tested locally on both sides but explicitly not deployed: routing/TLS not implemented (address null), customer execution gated off (verified-runtime policy empty), no deploy token issued. Note: this is about the managed (Hetzner) target. Building and running an AppBoundry application locally is available both through FeltKit and, without FeltKit, through `npx appport add` (FK-GAP-015).
evidence: appboundry docs/feltkit-deploy-readiness.md: 'Nothing here is deployed'; Routing 'designed, not implemented'; 'Untrusted execution in production: not ready'
feltkit docs/APPBOUNDRY-DEPLOY-CONTRACT.md: 'not deployed'
No APPBOUNDRY_URL / APPBOUNDRY_TOKEN in this environment
npx feltkit deploy --target appboundry (2026-11-05): '✗ Deploying to AppBoundry needs APPBOUNDRY_URL (the AppBoundry portal), APPBOUNDRY_TOKEN (an AppBoundry deploy token).'
https://appboundry.fly.dev/api/applications/multiplayer/hosting → HTTP 401 (portal up; contract's AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED)
gaps.wanted: A working public URL on the approved Hetzner target.
gaps.provided: feltkit build --target appboundry (artifact) and @appport/appboundry run (local runtime).
gaps.implementedManually: deploy/verify-appboundry.sh: builds the artifact and verifies it on the published runtime @appport/appboundry@1.8.0 (8/8 browser checks, restart recovery). No substitute hosting was provisioned.
gaps.workaround: Build the artifact and verify it on the published AppBoundry runtime locally; no invented deployment.
gaps.customLoc: 52 (deploy/verify-appboundry.sh 40 + deploy/check-persisted.ts 12) — verification, not a substitute deployment
gaps.proposal: Ship AppBoundry routing (§18), pin a verified runtime, issue a scoped deploy token.

gaps.title: No secure token / random primitive for application bearer secrets
gaps.description: Invitation links need an unguessable code. Record ids are `Date.now().toString(36) + randomBytes(6)` (48 random bits, timestamp prefix), and ctx offers no CSPRNG or token issuer that is guaranteed on both FeltKit's runtime and the AppBoundry WebAssembly guest (which removes ambient globals).
evidence: node_modules/@feltdb/feltkit/dist/runtime/data.js: export function newId() { return `${Date.now().toString(36)}${randomBytes(6).toString("hex")}`; }
appboundry docs/feltkit-deploy-readiness.md §3: guest has no ambient capability; host ABI is a closed set (db.*, outbox.stage, AppPort Services)
gaps.wanted: Invitation codes with >=128 bits of entropy, revocable, single use, that work on every runtime.
gaps.provided: Record ids (48 random bits). Sessions/API keys exist but are for principals, not app-level links.
gaps.implementedManually: Invitation = record id used as the code; single use, 7-day expiry, revocable, audited.
gaps.workaround: Accepted 48-bit codes, documented as a known limitation; mitigated by expiry, single use and revocation (no rate limiting).
gaps.codeFate: Invitation code generation would become one platform call; the invitation lifecycle stays app code.
gaps.proposal: ctx.crypto.token(bytes=32) (host-provided CSPRNG in both runtimes), or a platform 'link token' primitive: issue/verify/revoke a signed, expiring, single-use token bound to a record.

gaps.title: Client reconnect waits out exponential backoff (up to 10 s) after the network returns
gaps.description: After a network loss the change stream retries with backoff 0.5 s → 10 s and does not listen for the browser's online event, so a client that comes back online can wait up to ~10 s (measured 6.4–16 s in e2e) before re-querying. Durable recovery itself is correct: on reconnect every query re-runs.
evidence: client/index.ts #connect: delay = Math.min(delay * 2, 10_000); no 'online' listener
docs/screenshots/evidence.json: 'reconnection: offline session catches up' 6415 ms and 15963 ms in two runs
gaps.wanted: Catch up within ~1 s of the network returning.
gaps.proposal: Reset the backoff and reconnect on window 'online' and on visibilitychange→visible.

gaps.title: Capabilities require hand-written output schemas even when the handler's return type is known
gaps.description: Publishing a function as an AppPort capability requires `returns`; the loader refuses otherwise ('needs a returns schema: AppPort publishes and enforces its output contract'). This is a deliberate, correct contract rule with a clear error, but the schema restates what the TypeScript handler already returns. Classified as DX, not a defect.
evidence: FeltKitError CONFIGURATION: Capability "agent.pending" needs a `returns` schema
gaps.provided: Clear error; s.doc(collection) helps for stored records.
gaps.implementedManually: Return schemas for agent.pending/claim/context/fail and plans.get (~15 lines).
gaps.codeFate: Would shrink if returns could be derived from collection docs plus picks automatically; the contract itself should stay explicit.
gaps.proposal: None required; optionally a codegen hint that drafts the schema from the handler's inferred type.

gaps.title: FeltKit built-in accounts (sign-up / sign-in) are not available when the artifact runs on AppBoundry
gaps.description: The app declares auth: { accounts: { roles: ['member'] } }. Under feltkit dev/start, people sign up with e-mail and password. The same artifact on AppBoundry (production environment) reports 'sessions issued by operators only': /api/session has no `accounts`, and every user must be created with `appboundry admin users add` and given an operator-issued session. A self-serve collaboration product cannot onboard people on the approved target.
evidence: appboundry run output: 'Environment production (sessions issued by operators only)'
GET /api/session on the artifact: {devUsers: [], dashboard: null} — no accounts key; on feltkit dev the same call returns accounts: {signUp: true}
deploy/verify-appboundry.sh provisions ada/grace/assistant with appboundry admin users add + sessions issue
gaps.wanted: People sign up and accept an invitation link on the deployed app.
gaps.provided: Operator-provisioned users and sessions (AppBoundry admin CLI).
gaps.implementedManually: Nothing in the app; deployment script provisions identities by hand.
gaps.workaround: Operator issues sessions; the app's SessionForm (from the starter) accepts a pasted session.
gaps.customLoc: 0 app code; ~10 lines in deploy/verify-appboundry.sh provision users and sessions
gaps.proposal: AppBoundry: implement the accounts interface FeltKit's manifest declares (or delegate to AuthBoundry), so auth.accounts behaves the same on both runtimes; feltkit build should warn when the target cannot honour auth.accounts.
gaps.owner: AppBoundry (identity host interface); AuthBoundry as the eventual identity owner
gaps.status: open (blocks self-serve onboarding on the approved target)

gaps.title: MCP endpoint (and Studio) are not part of the artifact; agents on AppBoundry use HTTP only
gaps.description: feltkit build --target appboundry notes 'FeltKit Studio and the MCP endpoint are served by FeltKit, not by an artifact.' External agents that speak MCP cannot connect to the deployed app. The room agent works because it uses FeltKit's function API with an agent session, which AppBoundry serves.
evidence: feltkit build --target appboundry: '• Not in the artifact: FeltKit Studio (the development dashboard) and the MCP endpoint'
deploy/verify-appboundry.sh: room agent answers over HTTP on the artifact
gaps.wanted: Agents discover and invoke the app's capabilities over MCP wherever the app runs.
gaps.implementedManually: Room agent uses the HTTP client instead of MCP.
gaps.workaround: HTTP function API with an agent session.
gaps.proposal: AppBoundry serves /appport and /mcp from the manifest's AppPort contract (the capability set is already in manifest.json).

gaps.title: Two AppBoundry artifact formats and runtime paths: repository bundles (appport add) and FeltKit artifacts are not interchangeable
gaps.description: Any repository can become an AppBoundry application without FeltKit: `npx appport add` generates a contract, boundary and WASM crate; `npx appport app package` writes `<name>.app` (protocol AppPort/application-bundle/1: application.wasm + manifest), which `appboundry app install` and `appport app start` run (examples/todos: WASM execution units, external durable FeltDB state). FeltKit instead emits format appboundry.app/1 (manifest.json + module.wasm + assets), which `appboundry run` / `artifact verify` serve and which the FeltKit→AppBoundry deploy contract ships. `appboundry artifact verify` refuses the repository bundle (ARTIFACT_MANIFEST_MISSING). Two packaging contracts, two runtime entry points and two capability manifests for one control plane.
evidence: /tmp test 2026-11-05: npx appport add → 'Standalone AppPort setup complete', WASM sha256:ddde2a4e…; npx appport app package → multiplayer-direct.app (application.wasm, manifest: protocol AppPort/application-bundle/1)
appboundry artifact verify multiplayer-direct.app → 'error ARTIFACT_MANIFEST_MISSING: … has no manifest.json' (same for examples/todos/todos.app)
appboundry app install multiplayer-direct.app → 'Installed com.example.multiplayerdirect'
appport app start ./todos.app → 'Execution unit: exec_… Durable state: state_… (external)'
appboundry docs/contracts/feltkit-deploy/CONTRACT.md: the managed deploy contract is defined for the FeltKit artifact
gaps.wanted: One artifact contract that any producer (FeltKit, appport add in any language) emits and every AppBoundry runtime path (local run, install, Hetzner agent) accepts.
gaps.workaround: Use the FeltKit artifact path for this app.
gaps.proposal: Converge on one AppBoundry artifact contract (or make each runtime path accept both with one verifier), and make the managed deploy contract producer-neutral so `appport add` applications deploy the same way FeltKit ones do.

gaps.title: `npx appport add` is interactive-only and needs a Rust wasm32 toolchain
gaps.description: `appport add` asks for the application and each capability on a TTY. Piped stdin ends the run ('Detected unsettled top-level await', exit 13) because each prompt opens a new reader; no flags or file input were discoverable (`appport add --help` prints the top-level help). The WASM build then needs `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`; the CLI says so clearly and resumes without repeating setup.
evidence: printf answers | npx appport add → exits after 'Application ID' prompt with 'Warning: Detected unsettled top-level await'
driving prompts one at a time (tools: /tmp drive-add.cjs) completes; 'error The generated boundary is ready, but the WASM toolchain could not build it. Install Rust and the target…'
gaps.implementedManually: A small prompt driver for the comparison experiment (not part of the app).
gaps.proposal: `appport add --non-interactive --name … --capability name:in:out:perm` or `--from contract.json`; document the Rust requirement up front.

gaps.title: AppPort delivered events a session may not observe (wildcard subscriptions; subscriptions bypassed the application Authorizer)
gaps.description: A '*' subscription required no permission and received every event, including those whose definition requires permissions, contrary to spec §21.7. Subscription checks read session.permissions only, never the application's Authorizer. Found while closing FK-GAP-004.
evidence: packages/server/test/subscriptions.test.ts 'does not deliver events a wildcard subscriber may not observe' failed on e9815a5: received ['secrets.changed', 'news.posted'] for a principal without secrets.read
connection.ts (e9815a5) #subscribe: `const definition = name === "*" ? undefined : …; const required = definition?.authorization ?? []; const granted = this.#session?.permissions ?? []`
gaps.wanted: Events reach only sessions allowed to observe them.
gaps.implementedManually: Nothing in apps (FeltKit does not use AppPort events yet, so no FeltKit app was exposed).
gaps.proposal: Implemented: authorize subscribe and each delivery through the application's Authorizer.
gaps.status: fixed in AppPort locally (f1f8c21, unreleased, unpushed); needs review and release

gaps.title: AppPort decisions cannot conceal existence (no NOT_FOUND denial)
gaps.description: A policy that answers unknown and unauthorized ids alike (NOT_FOUND) cannot express it in AppPort's decision, which denies only with UNAUTHORIZED or FORBIDDEN.
evidence: @appport/authorization dist/index.d.ts: { allowed: false; code: 'UNAUTHORIZED' | 'FORBIDDEN'; reason? }
Multiplayer refuses cross-tenant ids with NOT_FOUND (tests/security.test.ts)
gaps.wanted: Refuse without revealing that the record exists.
gaps.implementedManually: FeltKit accepts fail('NOT_FOUND') thrown from the authorize hook and records it as a denial.
gaps.workaround: Throw instead of returning a decision.
gaps.proposal: Optional `NOT_FOUND` denial code (or `conceal: true`) on AuthorizationDecision.
